questions.question: Who among the following was one of the Congress leaders who drafted a Constitution for India in 1928?

__
 
• Motilal Nehru was one of the Congress leaders who drafted a** Constitution for India in 1928.**
 
• All Parties Conference convened by the Congress Party, appointed a Committee under Pandit Motilal Nehru to draft a Swaraj Constitution for India.
 
• The Nehru Committee worked from June to August 1928 and drafted a Constitution.
 
• This was the first Indian attempt at Constitution-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Somnath Lahiri **was an Indian statesman, writer and leader of the Communist Party of India.
 
• **Syama Prasad Mukherjee **was an Indian politician, barrister and academician, who served as the Minister for Industry and Supply in Jawaharlal Nehru's cabinet.

questions.question: Who among the following takes part in election of the President of India?

options.text: Elected Members of both the houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of the states.
Elected and nominated members of both the houses of Parliament.
Elected and nominated members of both the houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of the states.
Elected members of both the houses of Parliament only.

questions.solution:
__**Answer: (1)**__ - **Elected Members of both the Houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of the states.**

 
• The President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both the Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and the Union Territories of Delhi and Pondicherry.
 
• **Article 52** of the Constitution of India deals with the office of President.
 
• The manner of election of President is provided by** Article 55** of the Constitution.
 
• The general principle of the election of President is that the total number of votes cast by Member of Parliament equals the total number of votes cast by state legislators.
 
• **Part 5** of the Constitution under Chapter-1 (The Executive) lists out the qualification, election, and impeachment of the President of India (Article 52-Article 62).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India CANNOT be amended with simple majority?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 21** of the Constitution of India cannot be amended with a simple majority.
 
• Article 21 guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty, stating that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
 
• This article is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution and requires a more rigorous process for amendment as outlined in Article 368.
 
• Simple majority amendments are generally for non-fundamental aspects of the Constitution, whereas fundamental rights require a special majority and, in some cases, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles 2 and 3** relate to the admission or establishment of new states and the formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states, respectively. These can be amended with a simple majority.
 
• **Article 169** provides for the abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in states and can also be amended with a simple majority.
 
• The **Constitution** of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• The Constitution lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: As per the Constitution of India, the subject of 'livestock and animal husbandry' is included in the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State List:**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the Constitution of India, the subject of 'livestock and animal husbandry' is included in the **State List**__.
 
• There are 3 lists in the Indian Constitution, covered under the 7th schedule, these are the state, concurrent, and union list.
 
• The State list comprises of subjects under which laws could be made by the state legislature.
 
• The Union list covers subjects such as defence, railways, etc., under which the laws could be made by the Parliament.
 
• The Concurrent list covers subjects which give powers to both the state and central government.

questions.question: ________ of the Indian Constitution sets qualifications for being a member of Lok Sabha.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 84**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 84** of the Indian Constitution sets the qualifications required for being a member of the **Lok Sabha** (the House of the People, the lower house of Parliament).
 
• Key qualifications under **Article 84** include:
 
 
• The individual must be a citizen of India.
 
• They must be at least **25 years old**.
 
• They must possess other qualifications as may be prescribed by law made by Parliament, including not holding an office of profit under the government and being of sound mind.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 74**:

 
 
• Deals with the **Council of Ministers** to aid and advise the President.
 
• There shall be a **Council of Ministers**, with the **Prime Minister** at its head, to **aid and advise the President**.
 
• The President **shall act in accordance with such advice**, except where the Constitution explicitly requires otherwise.
 
 
 
• **Article 64**:
 
 
• The **Vice President of India** acts as the **ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States)**.
 
• The Vice President assumes this role automatically upon being elected as Vice President.
 
• In case of a tie during voting, the Vice President, as Chairman, exercises a **casting vote** to break the deadlock.
 
 
 
• **Article 76**:
 
 
• Relates to the **Attorney-General of India**.
 
• The** Attorney General is appointed by the President **of India and must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• This means the person must be a citizen of India and must have been an advocate for at least 10 years, a judge of a high court for 5 years, or an eminent jurist.

questions.question: The Bahujan Samaj Party was formed in 1984 under the leadership of ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**Kanshi Ram**__".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP)**,** a national political party in India, was formed in 1984. **
 
• **The BSP states that it represents the people at the lowest levels of the Hindu social system—those officially designated as members of the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes—as well as other religious** and **social minorities.**
 
• The core support group of the BSP consists primarily of the Dalits (**Scheduled** **Castes**, formerly called **untouchables**).
 
• The party espouses no specific ideology, other than its opposition to and outspoken criticism of the inequalities of the caste system, and its main tenets are focused on respecting and upholding the constitutional rights of the **lower members of Indian society.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**** **

 
• **Kanshi Ram (1934–2006),** a Dalit and a civil service worker, was spurred into pro-Dalit activism in the **1960s** after reading Ambedkar’s writings and through witnessing firsthand caste discrimination.
 
• Ram’s efforts to mobilize Dalits and other minorities led to his involvement in politics, in which he spent years crisscrossing Uttar Pradesh state and traveling throughout the country eliciting support for the cause.
 
• In 1984 he founded the party and led it until he was succeeded by** Kumari Mayawati in 2003.**
 
• Although Ram was responsible for building the support base for the party, Mayawati shaped and nurtured it into a powerful political force in **Uttar Pradesh**—India’s most populous state—and at the** national level.**
 
• The state long remained the **BSP’s** stronghold, and the party also has a presence in** Punjab state.**
 
• The first significant political success for the BSP came in 1993, when it entered into an alliance with the Samajwadi (Socialist) Party for the governance of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• In **1995**, however, the BSP left the coalition, and Mayawati, with support from **the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP),** became** chief minister **(head of government) in the state.
 
• Her first term lasted less than five months until the BJP withdrew its support.
 
• In the next several years Mayawati served two more short stints as chief minister: **6 months in 1997 and another 15 months in 2002–03.**

questions.question: To be elected as a member of the Legislative Council, a person should not be less than __________________ years of age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __30 years.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Members of a State Legislative Council (MLC) must be a citizen of India, at least **30 years old**, mentally sound, not insolvent, and must be enrolled voter of the state.
 
• Members of the Legislative Council (MLCs) are elected for a term of **six years, **with one-third of the members retiring every two years
 
• The** elections are conducted through a system of indirect election,** where members are elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, and local authority members in the state.
 
• The person should not be disqualified under the provisions of the Constitution, such as for being of unsound mind or having been convicted of certain offenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The **State Legislative Council** or **Vidhan Parishad** is the upper house in those states of India that have a **bicameral state legislature**; the lower house being the State Legislative Assembly.
 
• The Legislative Council of a state is constituted as per **Article 168 **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• As per **Article 171 **of the Indian Constitution, the total number of Members in the Legislative council of a State shall **not exceed one-third of the total number of Members** in the Legislative Assembly.
 
• Of the total number of Members of the Legislative Council, **1/3 of Members are elected by electorates** consisting of the Members of Local Authorities, **1/12 are elected by electorates consisting of graduates** residing in the State, **1/12 are elected by electorates consisting of persons engaged in teaching**, **1/3 are elected by the Members of Legislative Assembly** and the **remaining are nominated by the Governor.**

questions.question: The model of 'Quasi Federal' form of government in Indian constitution is borrowed from which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Canada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "Quasi Federal" refers to a system of governance that incorporates both federal and unitary elements.
 
• India's quasi-federal structure is inspired by the Canadian model of governance.
 
• Canada's constitution provides a federal system with a strong central government while allowing provincial autonomy.
 
• In the Indian context, the central government holds significant power, but states have their own jurisdiction over certain matters.
 
• This blend ensures a balance between the central authority and regional autonomy, similar to the Canadian federal system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federalism**

 
 
• A system of government where power is divided between a central authority and constituent political units.
 
• Promotes unity while accommodating regional diversity.
 
• Examples include the USA, Canada, Australia, and India.
 
 
 
• **Unitary System**
 
 
• A system of government where a single central authority holds the majority of the power.
 
• Local governments, if they exist, derive their authority from the central government.
 
• Examples include the United Kingdom and France.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List**
 
 
• In India's constitution, it comprises subjects where both the central and state governments can make laws.
 
• In case of conflict, central law prevails over state law.
 
• Examples of concurrent subjects include education, marriage and divorce, and bankruptcy and insolvency.
 
 
 
• **Residual Powers**
 
 
• Powers that are not explicitly listed in the constitution are granted to the central government.
 
• This concept ensures that the central government can legislate on new and unforeseen matters.

questions.question: In which of the following cases the Supreme Court, while laying out the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution held that the democratic character of the polity was an essential component of the ‘basic structure’?

options.text: Sajjan Singh vs State of Rajasthan
Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala
Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras
A K Gopalan vs State of Madras

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The case of Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala** in **1973** was a landmark decision that introduced the Basic Structure Doctrine into **Indian constitutional law**.
 
• This doctrine asserts that democracy founded on free and fair elections is a fundamental feature of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It serves as a safeguard, protecting the essential elements of the democratic system from arbitrary alterations or infringements.
 
• According to the** Basic Structure Doctrine, **any constitutional amendment that seeks to modify the basic structure of the Constitution is deemed invalid.
 
• This principle aims to uphold the integrity of Indian democracy and safeguard the rights and liberties of its citizens.
 
• **Justice Hans Raj Khanna **asserted that the constitution possesses a basic structure of constitutional principles and values.
 
• The 13-judge Constitution bench of the Supreme Court deliberated on the limitations, if any, of the powers of the elected representatives of the people and the nature of the fundamental rights of an individual.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 1965 case Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan** established the foundational principles of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **In the Romesh Thapar Case Verdict, **the Court determined that freedom of speech and expression encompasses the freedom to circulate ideas, ensuring their dissemination.
 
• **A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras**, AIR 1950 SC 27, was a significant ruling by the Supreme Court of India, where it clarified that Article 21 of the Constitution did not necessitate Indian courts to apply a due process of law standard.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with Official language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XVII**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XVII of the Indian Constitution deals with the Official Language**.
 
• It** includes Articles 343 to 351, **which outline provisions for the language to be used in the Union, States, and communication between them.
 
• It **also covers the promotion and development of the Hindi language** and the use of English alongside Hindi for official purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This part **deals with Miscellaneous Provisions of the Constitution.**
 
• It includes **Articles 361 to 367**, which cover topics such as the protection of the President
 
• It Governors from legal proceedings and the interpretation of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Part XVIII:**
 
 
• This part **deals with Emergency Provisions.**
 
• It includes **Articles 352 to 360, **which outline the types of emergencies in India: National Emergency, State Emergency (President’s Rule), and Financial Emergency.
 
• It** also describes the powers and procedures during these emergencie**s.
 
 
 
• **Part XVI:**
 
 
• This part is dedicated to **Special Provisions Relating to Certain Classes.**

questions.question: Right to Health is guaranteed to every citizen of India under which article?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Article 21**__ is one of the most expanded articles of the constitution of India and over the years it has brought out various derived rights under it.
 
• Article 21 provides the Right to Life and Personal Liberty and also includes:
 
 
• **Right to privacy.**
 
• Right to a good environment.
 
• Right to travel abroad.
 
• Right to sanitation.
 
• Right to a fair and speedy trial.
 
• Right to have a dignified life.
 
• **Right to health: State of Punjab V. Mohindar Singh Chawala, the apex court ruled that right to health is included under the ambit of right to life. This article also provides the right of patients to be treated with dignity, the right to medical confidentiality.**

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT come under the Concurrent List?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Artificial Habits**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Artificial Habitats**:

 
 
• **This topic is not explicitly mentioned in the Concurrent List.**
 
• **It generally pertains to environmental management and conservation measures, w**hich are primarily under the jurisdiction of the states.
 
• The** Indian Constitution divides legislative powers between the Centre and the States** through three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• The **Concurrent List** contains subjects on which both the **Centre and the States** can legislate.
 
• However, in case of any conflict, the law made by the **Central Government** prevails over the State law.
 
• This list contains areas of common interest where a unified legal framework might be beneficial, such as education, marriage laws, and social security.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medical Education**:

 
 
• This falls under the Concurrent List, allowing both the Centre and the states to legislate on this subject.
 
 
 
• **Protection of Wildlife**:
 
 
• This is also included in the Concurrent List, allowing both the central and state governments to take measures regarding wildlife protection.
 
 
 
• **Population Control**:
 
 
• This is part of the Concurrent List, where both levels of government can work together on policies and programs related to population management.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with Amendment of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XX.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Part XX of the Indian Constitution specifically addresses the **amendment procedures** for the Constitution.
 
• It lays down the process for amending various provisions of the Constitution, ensuring flexibility and adaptability to changing circumstances.
 
• The amendments **can be initiated in either house of Parliament** and require a majority vote to pass.
 
• **Some amendments require the approval of half of the state legislatures**, reflecting the federal structure of India.
 
• Part XX emphasizes the importance of maintaining the fundamental framework of the Constitution while allowing for necessary changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part XIX: Miscellaneous (Articles 361 to 367)**

 
 
• Part XIX of the Indian Constitution consists of provisions on the following aspects:
 
 
• Protection of the President and governors.
 
• Bar to interference by courts in disputes arising out of certain treaties, agreements, etc.
 
• Abolition of recognition of rulers of Indian states and privy purses.
 
• Special provisions as to major ports and aerodromes.
 
• Effect of failure to comply with or to give effect to directions given by the Union.
 
• Some definitions under Article 366.
 
• Interpretation of the constitutional provisions. 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Part XXI: Temporary, Transitional, and Special Provisions (Articles 369 to 392)**
 
 
• Part XXI of the Indian Constitution is a collection of legislation relating to the country’s Constitution and the union of states that constitutes it.
 
• Articles on Temporary, Transitional, and Special Provisions make up this section of the Constitution.
 
• Articles 371 to 371-J of Part XXI’s purpose is to meet the aspirations of the people of backward regions of the states, to protect the cultural and economic interests of the tribal people of the states, to deal with the disturbed law and order situation in some parts of the states, and to protect the interests of the local people of the states.
 
 
 
• **Part XXII: Short title, commencement, authoritative text in Hindi, and repeals (Articles 393 to 395)**
 
 
• Part XXII is a collection of legislation consisting of articles regarding the short title, date of commencement, authoritative text in Hindi, and repeals.

• In **1**934, M N Roy first proposed the idea of a constituent assembly.

questions.question:
Which among the following statements about judicial review in India are correct?

A. Judicial review means that the courts of law have the power of testing the validity of legislative as well as other governmental action with reference to the provisions of the Constitution.

B. Under Article 23 of the Indian Constitution, the compulsion of judicial review was described in the Fundamental Rights in Part III.

C. The power of judicial review is significantly vested upon the High Courts and the Supreme Court of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A and C only.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement A is** correct **because it defines the **concept of judicial review **and its scope in India.
 
• Statement B is** incorrect **because there is** no provision** in the Indian Constitution that describes the compulsion of judicial review in the Fundamental Rights in Part III.
 
• Statement C is **correct** because the power of judicial review is significantly vested upon the **High Courts and the Supreme Court **of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial review **is an important feature of the Indian Constitution that ensures the** supremacy of the Constitution **and the** rule of law**.
 
• The power of judicial review enables the judiciary to check the** abuse of power by the legislature** and the executive and to** protect the rights and liberties of the citizens.**
 
• The Indian Constitution's **Article 13 **outlines the procedures for judicial review.
 
• It requires the Indian State to** uphold and execute** the fundamental right.
 
• Additionally, it gives the courts the authority to declare a law or action** unconstitutional** if it violates a** fundamental right.**

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Indian National Congress make the demand for a Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1934**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An idea for a Constituent Assembly was proposed in 1934 by **M. N. Roy**, a pioneer of the Communist movement in India and an advocate of radical democracy.
 
• It became an official demand of the Indian National Congress in **1935**, the Indian National Congress held its session at **Lucknow **in** April 1936** presided by** Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru**. 
 
• With this, Congress added a new strand to its political engagement with the British on the future of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The official demand for Constituent Assembly was raised and the **Government of India Act, 1935** was **rejected **as it imposed the Constitution which was against the will of the Indians.
 
• **C. Rajagopalachari **voiced the demand for a Constituent Assembly on 1**5 November 1939** based on adult franchise and was accepted by the British in **August 1940**.
 
• On **8 August 1940**, a statement was made by **Viceroy Lord Linlithgow** about the expansion of the **Governor-General's Executive Council** and the establishment of a War Advisory Council.
 
• This offer, known as the **August Offer**, included giving full weight to minority opinions and allowing Indians to draft their own constitution.
 
• Under the** Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946**, **elections were held for the first time **for the Constituent Assembly.
 
• The Constitution of India was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, and it was implemented** under the Cabinet Mission Plan** on **16 May 1946**.
 
• The members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by the provincial assemblies by a single, transferable-vote system of proportional representation.
 
• The total membership of the Constituent Assembly was **389 **of which **292 **were representatives of the provinces, **93 **represented the princely states and four were from the chief commissioner provinces of Delhi, Ajmer-Merwara, Coorg, and British Baluchistan.

• **Sixth Schedule**

 
 
• The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution provides for the administration of tribal areas in **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram** to safeguard the rights of the tribal population in these states.
 
• This special provision for these autonomous council is provided under **Article 244(2) and Article 275(1)** of the Constitution.
 
• **Presently, 10 Autonomous Councils** in Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura are formed by virtue of the Sixth Schedule.
 
 
 
• **The Chakma Autonomous District Council**
 
 
• The Chakma Autonomous District Council is an autonomous council for the Chakma people living in the south-western part of Mizoram, India.
 
• It covers the Tuichawng (Chawngte) subdivision of the Lawngtlai district.
 
• Its headquarters is at Kamalanagar.
 
• The Chakma people have been demanding to change the status of the **Chakma Autonomous District Council** into a Union territory under the name **Chakmaland**.

questions.question: According to Hindu calendar, the Indian Constitution came into force on?
questions.solution:
The Indian Constitution came into force on Margsheersh Shukla Saptami, Samvat 2006 Vikrami.

 
• As per the English calendar, it came into force on 26th January 1950.
 
• It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949.

questions.question: The _______ provides for measures to deter fugitive economic offenders from evading the process of law in India by staying outside the jurisdiction of Indian courts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018:-

 
 
• An Act to provide for measures to deter fugitive economic offenders from evading the process of law in India by staying outside the jurisdiction of Indian courts, to preserve the sanctity of the rule of law in India, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. 
 
• An FEO is defined by The Fugitive Economic Offenders (FEO) Act, 2018 as “any individual against whom a warrant for arrest in relation to a scheduled offence has been issued by any court in India, who
 
 
• (i) has left India so as to avoid criminal prosecution; or
 
• (ii) abroad refusing to return to India to face criminal prosecution”.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Offenders Act, 2018 **is an incorrect option as there is no such act. The correct name of the act is the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018.
 
• **Fugitive Offenders Act, 2015** is an incorrect option as it is a Hong Kong law that allows the extradition of fugitives to mainland China, which has faced criticism for violating human rights.
 
• **Foreign Economic Offenders Act, 2018** is an incorrect option as there is no such act.
